summary: Backend-only testing of FortexaRH P2 (iter 238): UK HMRC RTI FPS XML + FR DSN XML + Fiscal Calendar dashboard. 48/48 tests PASSED. Validated: (1) Catalog now reports implemented_formats=12 (DO=4, CO=1, MX=2, US=1, ES=2, GB=1, FR=1); GB and FR have compliance_status='complete'; 21 non-implemented countries remain universal_only. (2) Country guard for /gb/rti-fps and /fr/dsn returns 400 with helpful messages when company.country!=GB/FR; returns 200 application/xml when correctly set. (3) RTI FPS XML: starts with <?xml, root GovTalkMessage in namespace http://www.govtalk.gov.uk/CM/envelope, filename RTI_FPS_*.xml, contains <FullPaymentSubmission>, <EmpRefs> (OfficeNo/PayeRef/AOref), and each <Employee> has <EmployeeDetails> (NINO where available, Name/Fore/Sur), <Employment> with <PaymentToDate> (TaxablePay, TaxDeducted, EmployeeNICsInPeriod, EmployerNICsInPeriod, NetPay). (4) DSN XML: root <DSN> with version='P24V01', filename DSN_*.xml, contains <Declaration> (Nature/Type/MoisPrincipal), <Emetteur> (SIREN/NIC), <Entreprise> (SIREN/APE), <Etablissement> (SIRET/APE), per-employee <Salarie> with <NIR>, <Nom>, <Prenoms>, <Contrat>, <Remuneration> (MontantBrut), <Cotisation> with codes 100/200/400/900, <VersementIndividuel>, final <BordereauCotisation>. (5) Both endpoints return 404 for empty period (2099-12). (6) /api/native-reports/calendar returns today (ISO), company_country, total_upcoming=12, next_due (first item of deadlines sorted asc by days_until_due), deadlines[], by_country dict containing all 7 implemented countries with correct counts (DO=4, MX=2, ES=2, CO=1, US=1, GB=1, FR=1), summary (overdue/critical/warning/ok). Urgency mapping (<0 overdue, <=3 critical, <=7 warning, >7 ok) holds for every item; summary counts match. is_company_country flag flips correctly when country is changed (DO -> GB). Every deadline item has the required 14 keys (country_code, country_name, flag, format_code, format_name, agency, frequency, due_date, days_until_due, period_to_file, description, endpoint, is_company_country, urgency) with correct types. (7) REGRESSION: All 31 previously-passing tests from iter 237 (catalog, country guard, DO/CO/MX/US/ES generation + 404 cases, auth, iter_235 cost-comparison/PDF/fiscal-summary) still PASS. CRITICAL: session-scoped autouse fixture restored company.country to 'DO' at end of run; verified post-run via GET /api/country-config/company -> country_code='DO'.
critical_code_review_comments: native_reports.py:1006  <PeriodEnd> is hardcoded to day '30' every month, which is wrong for February (28/29) and April/June/September/November (30 is fine) but not consistent with monthrange; use calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1] to compute last-day-of-month. Not breaking schema validation today but HMRC would flag '2026-02-30'.

native_reports.py:1056  RTI FPS <PmtDate> is hardcoded to day 25 — should come from the period's actual pay_date (period_info contains it) to reflect real HMRC payroll timing; hardcoded value makes YTD/FY-boundary logic incorrect.
native_reports.py:1181  DSN <DateFinPaie> uses literal '30' — fails for February and produces an invalid date. Use calendar.monthrange to derive last-day-of-month.

native_reports.py:1187-1190  DSN Cotisation amounts are split using hardcoded percentages (0.3/0.5/0.05/0.15) on top of the aggregated ss_emp/ss_er. These are approximations and do not sum to 100% (0.3+0.5=0.8 for employee; 0.4+0.4+0.05+0.15=1.0 for employer). The employee side silently loses 20% of cotisations. Either balance the split or document it as illustrative.
native_reports.py:1104  period_dsn computed but never used — dead variable.

native_reports.py:1232-1244  FORMAT_DEADLINES uses a simple {day, offset_months} schema that ignores business-day conventions (UK HMRC deadlines roll to the next working day; US Form 941 has 10-day grace when all deposits were made on time; Mexico IMSS is 17th but rolls to next business day). Document as 'statutory nominal date' and expose a field for grace/business-day rolling later.

native_reports.py:1282  For monthly formats the calendar computes deadlines against the current calendar month, but the 'period_to_file' uses offset_months subtraction. For INFONAVIT (bimonthly, offset_months=2) the period_to_file may land on the wrong bimester when today is in the 'off' month. Add explicit bimester logic.

native_reports.py:949 _xml_pretty uses minidom.toprettyxml which re-emits an <?xml?> declaration; the caller works around this with .split('\n', 1)[1]. Cleaner to use ET.tostring(xml_declaration=True) directly or pass standalone='yes'.
native_reports.py:1083-1223 generate_fr_dsn is ~140 lines — extract _build_dsn_salarie(emp, totals, month, year) and _build_dsn_cotisations(totals) to reduce complexity and aid unit testing.

native_reports.py size = 1338 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline; split into co_pila.py, mx_reports.py, us_form941.py, es_reports.py, gb_rti_fps.py, fr_dsn.py, calendar.py under /app/backend/routes/native/ so each file is < 300 lines.

calendar endpoint performs a DB fetch for company_country but does not verify the user has a company; if company_id is missing, company_country silently defaults to 'DO' — consider 404 when no company is bound to the current user.

GB NINO field defaults to empty if missing; the code guards by only emitting <NINO> when non-empty, which is correct, but HMRC RTI validation WILL reject an FPS without NINO unless a valid substitute (date-of-birth fallback) is provided. Document or add a validation error.
DSN NIR default is '1000000000000' (placeholder) — URSSAF would reject this. Raise 422 when any employee lacks a NIR for FR filings instead of filing with a fake number.
seed_data_creation: None. Reused existing paid period 2026-03 (period_42a51c051530). No employees/periods added or removed. Country flipped DO -> GB/FR/etc during tests and restored to DO in autouse teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Native Fiscal Reports P2 (GB RTI FPS + FR DSN + Calendar) is fully validated. /app/backend/tests/test_native_reports.py now contains 48 reusable tests across 11 classes: TestCatalog [8], TestCountryGuard [3], TestColombiaPILA [2], TestMexicoIMSS [4], TestUSForm941 [4], TestSpainModelo111 [2], TestSpainTC1 [2], TestNativeReportsAuth [2], TestRegressionIter235 [4], TestCatalogGBFRComplete [2], TestGBRtiFps [4], TestFrDsn [4], TestFiscalCalendar [7]. Implemented formats = 12 (DO=4, CO=1, MX=2, US=1, ES=2, GB=1, FR=1); 21 countries remain universal_only. When adding a new format, increment implemented_formats expectation in test_catalog_basic_shape, add to TestFiscalCalendar.test_calendar_by_country_contains_all_7_implemented expected counts, and add deadline to FORMAT_DEADLINES dict. Calendar endpoint is country-independent (reads all implemented formats) but reads company_country and marks is_company_country; verified that changing company country flips the flag. Session-scoped autouse fixture restore_country_to_do guarantees company.country='DO' after the suite (verified post-run). RTI FPS and DSN XMLs validated for well-formedness via ET.fromstring and for structural completeness via substring checks on required element tags (because ElementTree folds namespaces into Clark notation).
rca of the issue: N/A — all 48 tests passed on second run, no issues found. The only first-run failure was a test-side bug in my assertion (ElementTree folds xmlns into tag as Clark notation {ns}tag, so root.get('xmlns') is None); fixed by asserting on either namespace prefix in root.tag or xmlns attribute.
